drafted_from: tool:list-the-facebook-pages-a-sign-in-reaches's row in tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/tool-rows.json (job, description, input_schema, invoke) and the folder's test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs, whose stand-in answers give the reply and the held word
start_here: Say to your AI: "List the Facebook Pages a sign-in reaches for the new connection service_connection:facebook-messenger:7d3c88e1 with the code made-up-code-4f9a2c." It runs tool:list-the-facebook-pages-a-sign-in-reaches and tells you the tokens are kept in the vault without showing any of them.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it sends one request to Facebook for the connection it is handed and keeps the tokens in the vault as that connection's fields.
instructions: 1. Do not run this by hand: tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service runs it for you at the sign-in callback, after you open the sign-in address it gave you. Start that tool first (its kit shows the call) and keep the connection_id it answers: service_connection:facebook-messenger:7d3c88e1 is the shape.

2. To run this step alone, the AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:list-the-facebook-pages-a-sign-in-reaches and the input the worked example shows (the connection by its handle only).

3. Read what comes back: the service's reply with every kept token already replaced by the word [held]. Nothing is kept: no Page token is read here. The connect tool picks the Page the person named beforehand (or the only one) and then runs the keep step for it.
4. A refusal (a used-up code, a wrong callback address) is shown as the service's own error; nothing is kept, so start the sign-in again for a new link.
